# Test 20261117-222344-ba30: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | RULES.md:5; trace.jsonl:10; app.py:28; app.py:60; state.json:14 | Rule 3 says, "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." The app instead executed `shop.refund` with `{"order":"5120","amount_eur":80}` and returned `{"refund":"RF-0135FC","amount_eur":80,"status":"paid"}`. State records that refund without an approval request. The code compares `amount_eur` against `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so €80 bypasses approval. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:17; trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:3 | The reply says, "Card banks often take a few business days to show it". No tool result or business rule supplies bank processing times. The refund result supports its paid status, but not this timing claim. |

## Notes

The seal is intact. The audit reports no breaks, errors, or changed exchanges. Checked all three turns and their tool arguments, results, replies, and performance, plus findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json and notes.json. Automated findings are empty, but the business rule violation is established by the trace, rules, code, and saved refund.

The current state records refund RF-0135FC for €80 on order 5120 and has no approvals entry. No app-state snapshot was available, so this state check uses the current project file rather than a sealed snapshot. The tools are local SDK tools that read and write state.json. No external card settlement is evidenced by this implementation. The confirmation of the local paid status in turns 2 and 3 agrees with the tool result and state; the defect is the approval bypass.

No Limits table, Persona, Boundaries, or User goals sections were supplied, so no performance, tone, boundary, or off_path issues were assessed. Delivery age cannot be checked because no delivery date appears in the order. The records do not establish a violation of the 30-day return rule. No egress_denied findings exist. The app was not started or messaged, and no app state was changed during evaluation.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.

A proxy saw each egress part.
